**What I found about Medardo Joseph Mazombwe:**
- He was a Zambian Cardinal of the **Catholic Church** (not a different religion he wanted to reform - he was already a Catholic leader)
- He was born September 24, 1931, and died August 29, 2013 in Lusaka, Zambia
- He served as Archbishop of Lusaka (1996-2006) and Bishop of Chipata (1970-1996)

My searches revealed references to Mazombwe's connection to the **"Częstochowa Statement"** (also spelled Czestochowa), which is a document related to **authentic Marian devotion**. - **The District**: If referring to **Sandomierz** (the diocese associated with Częstochowa Statement), it's located in **southern Poland** in the Świętokrzyskie Voivodeship

If this question refers to someone preaching Marian devotion before death in connection with Mazombwe's religious reforms, the most likely district answer is **Sandomierz** (in the **Świętokrzyskie region of Poland**), since:

**Medardo Joseph Mazombwe** (24 September 1931 – 29 August 2013) was a [cardinal of the Catholic Church] "Cardinal (Catholicism)"). He was Zambia's first indigenous cardinal.[[1]]

He was the former archbishop of the [Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Lusaka] (1996–2006)[[2]] and Bishop of the [Roman Catholic Diocese of Chipata] (1970–1996).

[Pope Benedict XVI] elevated Mazombwe to the status of [Cardinal-Priest] "Cardinal (Catholicism)") of _[Santa Emerenziana a Tor Fiorenza]_ at a [consistory] on 20 November 2010.[[3]]

He held several senior positions in the local and regional church, such as [Zambia Episcopal Conference] president (1972–1975; 1988–1990; 1999–2002), and as chairman of the regional conferences under [Association of Member Episcopal Conferences in Eastern Africa] (A.M.E.C.E.A.) (1979–86). He was an ardent campaigner for Zambia's [debt cancellation] in the mid-1980s, through the Jubilee movement campaign and spearheaded several new developmental projects in many parts of the country including the Mumpanshya area of [Chongwe].[[4]]

## Legacy

[[edit]]

After his death, a foundation and a school were named after him in Chipata.[[5]]

- He was a Zambian Cardinal of the **Catholic Church** (not a different religion he wanted to reform - he was already a Catholic leader)
- He was born September 24, 1931, and died August 29, 2013 in Lusaka, Zambia
- He served as Archbishop of Lusaka (1996-2006) and Bishop of Chipata (1970-1996)

**The Marian Devotion Connection:**
My searches revealed references to Mazombwe's connection to the **"Częstochowa Statement"** (also spelled Czestochowa), which is a document related to **authentic Marian devotion**. The Częstochowa Statement comes from the **Diocese of Sandomierz** in **Poland**, where Marian devotion has deep historical roots dating back to the Middle Ages.

- **A Polish figure**: The Częstochowa Statement originated in Poland, so there may be a Polish priest/figure who preached on Marian devotion before dying

If this question refers to someone preaching Marian devotion before death in connection with Mazombwe's religious reforms, the most likely district answer is **Sandomierz** (in the **Świętokrzyskie region of Poland**), since:
